en: The *Narmadāṣṭaka* composed by the illustrious Ādi Śaṅkarācārya: [O Narmadā],
you who are adorned by the breaking waves of the ocean with its drops,
and who are joined with waters that act as enemies to the multitude of sins of your detractors.
O Goddess Narmadā, I bow to your lotus feet, which dispel the fear of Kṛtānta, Dūtaka, Kāla, and Bhūta, O bestower of armor (protection). 1.

To you, who are the divine bestower of the tradition of the fish and the river, who remove the heavy burden of the flood of impurities in the Kali age, the leader of all sacred fords, and the granter of happiness to the multitude of excellent fish,
tortoises, crocodiles, and ruddy geese;
O Goddess Narmadā, I bow to your lotus-feet.
To the one who has swept away the earth with the flood of his great and deep waters, who has shattered the mountain of calamities by slaying all the enemies of sin,
and who dwells in the palace of Mṛkaṇḍu’s son amidst the great terror of the world's dissolution; I bow.
O Goddess Narmadā, I bow to your lotus-like feet.
My fear departed at that very moment when I beheld your water,
which is ever served by the son of Mṛkaṇḍu, by Śaunaka, and by the enemy of the Asuras;
it is the source of birth in the ocean of rebirth and the armor against the suffering of the ocean of worldly existence.
O Goddess Narmadā, I bow to your lotus-like feet.
Worshipped by countless lakhs of kinnaras, gods, asuras, and others; resounding with the warbling of hundreds of wise birds on the beautiful banks of the river;
bestowing bliss upon Vasiṣṭha, Śiṣṭa, Pippalāda, Kardama, and the rest.
O Goddess Narmadā, I bow to your lotus-feet.

Sustained within their own minds by Sanatkumāra, Nāciketa, Kaśyapa, Atri, and the six sages, as well as by Nārada and the other six, [this work] bestows the merit of the deeds of Ravi, Indu, Antideva, and Devarāja.
O Goddess Narmadā, I bow to your lotus feet.
Then [he beheld] that which is the weapon of the essence of millions upon millions of sins,
yet the thread of life for all living beings, the bestower of both worldly enjoyment and liberation,
and the armor of the abodes of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva.
I bow to your lotus-feet, O Goddess Narmadā.

Oh, what nectar-like sound has been heard on the crest of the matted locks of Maheśa— [a sound] which removes the torment of inexhaustible sins and bestows happiness upon all beings, [even among] the Kirātas, Sūtas, Vāḍabas, the learned, the rogue, and the actor!
O Goddess Narmadā, I bow to your lotus-like feet.
But those who always recite this *Narmadāṣṭaka* at the three times of day never, without exception, go to an evil state of existence.
Rare is the attainment of this human body; rare is the majesty of the abode of Maheśa.
Men who are subject to rebirth certainly do not behold Raurava.
Thus ends the *Narmadāṣṭaka*, composed by the venerable Ādi Śaṅkarācārya. O Narmadā, take [my sins] away! O Narmadā, take [my sins] away! O Narmadā, take [my sins] away!
